summary.intent: Drive Callisto PRs #634 (change #242), #638 (#246) and #645 (#253) to a state with zero reviewer findings, using Codex's closure plan and verification reports, then have the owner merge them and release #628.
summary.outcome: Three parallel workstreams ran: #246 (0992460d7) and the #253 split (ce3b37054) were pushed, and #253 got a further env-test fix (H3K46V) committed, pushed and resolved. #242 has four fixes committed locally and its gate and targeted Codex review are still pending, so it is not pushed. A spike was launched for the push-destination defects that already exist on main.

repo: Gate is `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test`, plus `just fuzz-check` when callisto-model public signatures change. Judge by exit code.

Passing CI and 225 focused tests did not catch Codex's reproduced defects, so a bare `codex review` is not a sufficient oracle. Targeted reviews need explicit failure cases, positive controls and failing tests.

Four push-destination defects (double URL rewrite, extra push URLs dropped, canonicalization altering the repo path, push.followTags publishing unrelated tags) already exist on main and are not introduced by #253. They need a separate spiked change.

Process-count tests must use tags for older versions. Moving the same current-version tag to an older commit still triggers commit resolution. Modern git's peeled-tag cache can make a no-lookup assertion vacuous, so force a cache miss and add a positive control.

Stderr advisory, error-card and subprocess-echo writes should go through one best-effort boundary. Prompts, review output, storage writes and real process failures must stay fallible, and a failed echo must not stop draining child output.
Hazardous package names (whitespace, commas) are handled with a rows-only selection mode, implemented once in `tty` and shared by `add` and `init`.
`init` must write callisto.toml only after the README succeeds, otherwise a retry fails with 'already initialized'.
Tests must not print full child environments on failure because that can leak secrets into CI logs. Assert on named variables only.

code.finding: The runner env test printed the entire child `env` stdout when a policy variable was missing or wrong. The runner strips only known credential variables, so unrelated secrets could leak into logs (finding H3K46V). The assertion now names only the missing variable.

workflow: Each push triggers a paid review, so batch all fixes and push once per PR, and push only after a gated, Codex-clean commit.
Spawn separate `claude --bg` sessions in separate worktrees for each workstream, and have one integrator merge the corrected heads. Integration done on old heads is not readiness evidence.
The permission classifier blocks `gh pr close` and `pkill` on shared processes. Get the user's explicit OK or use TaskStop on your own task instead.
Close findings as stale or resolved with a stated reason, and check whether a finding's file still exists after a split.
The user wants decisions and recommendations rather than option surveys, and does not want reversals on questions. Questions from the user are not orders.

friction: Repeated owner frustration over new findings after each push, paid reviews, flip-flopping and slow progress.
Checking the #253 remote head timed out once, so it needed a recheck.
The user asked to push while the sessions were still mid-work, and there was nothing gated to push.
My earlier plan was too thin: it misjudged the test fix, the #253 closure and the integration scope, and needed Codex's corrections.
The release-hardening suite stalled during Codex's verification and was recorded as incomplete.

Merge order: #246, then #242, then #253 (or the reduced #253). The owner merges, and #645 closure was previously awaiting the user's OK.
Refresh release PR #628 (0.23.0) from final main and verify its Breaking/Action items, CI and approval.
Run an independent accumulated-diff review with Codex's checklist.
